name: Handmade Woven Bilum Bag
short: Traditional bilum, hand-woven by Highland artisans.
description: A beautifully hand-woven bilum bag crafted with traditional Highland techniques. Each piece is unique and made with natural fibres, combining heritage with everyday practicality.

name: Highland Coffee Beans (500g)
short: Fresh-roasted single origin from the Highlands.
description: Rich, aromatic single-origin coffee grown in the Papua New Guinea highlands and roasted in small batches for peak freshness. 500g whole beans.

name: Hand-carved Wooden Bowl
short: Solid wood bowl with traditional Sepik carvings.
description: A deep, hand-carved bowl made from locally-sourced timber. The exterior features traditional Sepik-inspired motifs. Perfect as a centrepiece or fruit bowl.

name: Traditional Shell Necklace
short: Statement necklace made from polished shells.
description: A handcrafted necklace made from polished cowrie and bailer shells — a symbol of wealth and status in many PNG coastal cultures. Each piece is one of a kind.

name: Organic Gift Basket
short: Seasonal fruit, coffee and honey in a woven basket.
description: A thoughtfully curated basket of seasonal produce, PNG-roasted coffee, and local honey, wrapped in a reusable woven basket. Perfect gift.

name: Sepik River Clay Pot
short: Hand-thrown ceremonial pot from the Sepik.
description: A hand-thrown clay pot modelled on traditional ceremonial vessels from the Sepik River region. Fired using age-old methods. Each pot is signed by the artisan.

name: Grass-woven Storage Basket
short: Durable, woven storage basket for everyday use.
description: A sturdy, hand-woven storage basket made from locally harvested grass. Great for laundry, toys, or decorative storage. Natural variations make each one unique.

name: Local Tour Guide Service
short: Half-day guided tour with a local expert.
description: A half-day walking tour led by a knowledgeable local guide. Discover hidden markets, cultural sites, and the stories behind the neighbourhood. Price is per person.
